slide_title: Independent Assortment and Segregation During Meiosis
original_text: Independent Assortment and Segregation During Meiosis
explanation: Independent assortment and segregation of chromosomes during meiosis I explain the physical basis of Mendel's laws. The alignment of homologous chromosomes at the metaphase plate is random, leading to diverse combinations of maternal and paternal chromosomes in gametes.

questions.q: During which phase of cell division do independent assortment and segregation of homologous chromosomes physically occur?
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the random alignment of homologous chromosomes occurs during Metaphase I and their separation occurs during Anaphase I of Meiosis I.
